headline: A junior minister's late-night tweet sparks a minor row
body: A backbench-turned-minister's reply to a critic gets screenshotted and goes round Westminster Twitter before breakfast.

actions.label: Distance the party from the remark

effects.summary: A swift, mild rebuke draws a line under it within a day.

actions.label: Defend the minister and move on

effects.summary: Critics accuse the leadership of tin ears; the story runs a day longer than it should.

actions.label: Say nothing and let it blow over

effects.summary: It blows over by the next news cycle, as these usually do.

headline: Flooding hits a market town overnight
body: Heavy rain overwhelms drainage in a small town; the council and emergency services pull an all-nighter on sandbags and rescues.

effects.summary: Local services are praised for a quick response; no national ripple.

headline: Monthly economic figures land — mixed picture
body: Growth, inflation and unemployment numbers are released; commentators find a story in them either way.

effects.summary: The numbers keep the economy in the headlines for another news cycle.

headline: A clip of an MP goes viral for the wrong reasons
body: Ten seconds of an awkward committee-room answer gets clipped, captioned, and shared a few hundred thousand times.

actions.label: Have the MP laugh it off online

effects.summary: A good-natured response turns mockery into mild affection.
The clip fades within a couple of days, as most do.

headline: A new opinion poll is published
body: The latest voting-intention poll lands, folding in everything that's happened since the last one.

headline: A ward by-election result lands quietly
body: A routine council by-election, caused by a resignation, returns a result nobody outside the ward much notices.

effects.summary: Barely registers beyond the local paper.
